slides.title: *Domain* vs *Data element*
slides.subtitle: Explain it clearly in 30 seconds. Swipe.

slides.heading: *Domain* = technical
slides.body:
Defines how the value is stored: data type, length, decimals.

Also fixed values, value table and conversion routine (like ALPHA).

slides.heading: *Data element* = meaning
slides.body:
Defines what the field means: field labels, F1 documentation, search help.

It points to a domain (or a built-in type) for the technical details.

slides.heading: Real example: *KUNNR*
slides.code:
Table field  KNA1-KUNNR
  Data element  KUNNR
    Labels: "Customer"
  Domain        KUNNR
    CHAR 10
    Conversion   ALPHA
slides.note: One domain can be reused by many data elements with different labels.

slides.heading: How to *answer it*
items: Give the one-line difference - Domain is technical, data element is semantic
Name what each holds - Type and length vs labels and F1 help
Add a real example - KUNNR with ALPHA conversion

posts.caption:
"What is the difference between a domain and a data element?"

A simple way to answer:
- Domain: the technical side. Data type, length, decimals, fixed values, conversion routine.
- Data element: the meaning. Field labels, F1 documentation, search help. It refers to a domain.

Then give a real example, such as KUNNR with its ALPHA conversion. That one detail shows you have actually worked in SE11.

Save this before your next interview.

slides.title: Find where *any error message* comes from
slides.subtitle: In under a minute
slides.voiceover: यूज़र को कोई एरर मैसेज आ रहा है, और आपको पता ही नहीं कि ये कहाँ से आ रहा है? ये ट्रिक सीख लो।
slides.spoken: User ko koi error message aa raha hai, aur aapko pata hi nahi ki ye kahan se aa raha hai? Ye trick seekh lo.

slides.heading: The *problem*
slides.body:
A standard transaction shows an error.

Thousands of lines of code. Which one raised it?
slides.highlight: Searching the code by hand takes hours
slides.voiceover: स्टैंडर्ड ट्रांज़ैक्शन में हज़ारों लाइन्स का कोड होता है। हाथ से ढूंढोगे, तो घंटों लग जाएंगे।
slides.spoken: Standard transaction mein hazaaron lines ka code hota hai. Haath se dhoondhoge, to ghanton lag jaayenge.

slides.heading: Step 1: *Start the debugger*
items: Type /h in the command field - Press Enter
Repeat the action - The debugger opens
Open Breakpoints menu - Breakpoint at Statement
slides.voiceover: सबसे पहले कमांड फील्ड में स्लैश एच टाइप करो, और एंटर दबाओ। अब वही एक्शन दोबारा करो। डीबगर खुल जाएगा। फिर ब्रेकपॉइंट्स मेन्यू में जाओ।
slides.spoken: Sabse pehle command field mein slash h type karo aur Enter dabao. Ab wahi action dobara karo. Debugger khul jaayega. Phir Breakpoints menu mein jao.

slides.heading: Step 2: *Breakpoint at MESSAGE*
items: Debugger stops at the exact line - Before the message shows
Check the IF above it - That is your root cause
slides.voiceover: ब्रेकपॉइंट एट स्टेटमेंट में मैसेज लिखो, और एफ़ एट दबाओ। डीबगर ठीक उसी लाइन पर रुकेगा, जहाँ से मैसेज आ रहा है। अब ऊपर वाली कंडीशन देखो। वही असली वजह है।
slides.spoken: Breakpoint at statement mein MESSAGE likho aur F8 dabao. Debugger theek usi line par rukega jahan se message aa raha hai. Ab upar wali condition dekho. Wahi asli wajah hai.

slides.title: Save this for your *next bug*
slides.body: Daily ABAP tips, code and interview questions.
slides.voiceover: ये ट्रिक प्रोडक्शन इश्यूज़ में बहुत काम आती है। पोस्ट सेव करो, और फॉलो करो अबैप कोड वॉल्ट।
slides.spoken: Ye trick production issues mein bahut kaam aati hai. Post save karo aur follow karo ABAP Code Vault.

posts.caption:
A user reports an error, and you have no idea which line of code raised it.

The fastest way to find out:
1. Type /h in the command field and press Enter
2. Repeat the action to open the debugger
3. Breakpoints > Breakpoint at Statement > MESSAGE
4. Press F8. The debugger stops at the exact line.

Look at the condition above that line. That is usually your root cause.

Save this for your next production issue.
